exposure: concern about the cost associated with cesarean section
perception that a cesarean section affects body image
outcome: preferred mode of delivery (trial of labor or cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 169 pregnant women with one previous cesarean scar and nonrecurring indications for C-section, attending antenatal care in two public hospitals in Uganda.
finding: The desire to have more children and concern about medical expenses increased the likelihood of preferring a vaginal birth, while body image concerns and being employed increased the likelihood of a cesarean section preference.
mod_finding: Trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) was preferred by 81% of women, with desire for more children and concern for costs increasing TOLAC preference, while body image concerns and employment increased C-section preference.
